AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: Queen.cs:125-130 does exactly two things: caches `Amalgam = CombatState.Enemies.First(c => c.Monster is TorchHeadAmalgam)` and sets the 'queen_progress' music parameter to 1f. The music half is presentation (SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 waives NRunMusicController). The cache half is DEAD STATE in the source: `Amalgam` is written at Queen.cs:128 and nulled at :227 and is READ NOWHERE in the file -- every decision goes through HasAmalgamDied instead. The sim drops the field and resolves the amalgam live in _amalgam() whenever a condition needs it, which is the same observable. Note this is NOT the shared constructor-power finding: the Queen applies no starting power, so SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 does not apply and this entry stands on its own reading. One divergence the live lookup introduces and the cache does not: C#'s `.First(...)` THROWS if the encounter contains no amalgam, while the sim's loop returns None and _amalgam_died() then reports True, sending the Queen straight to OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD. Dormant on both sides -- QUEEN_BOSS is the Queen's only encounter and always pairs her with a TorchHeadAmalgam (queen.py:217-223, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :193-196, unchanged), matching the C# boss.

AfterDeath.issue: Closed 2026-07-28: the Queen now has a real AfterDeath listener. RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-04: the mechanism has been simplified further since -- hook_dispatch/G5 gave the sim a real MonsterModel listener category (the Monster IS its own listener, monsters/base.py:186), so the private `_AmalgamDeathListener` this issue originally described is GONE; `Queen.on_death` (queen.py:102-110) is now the direct listener body, unchanged in effect. Its on_death fires Queen.on_amalgam_died (queen.py:113-123), which -- when the pending move is BURN_BRIGHT_FOR_ME_MOVE -- runs `machine.force_current_state(ENRAGE_MOVE)` plus `_current_move = enraged`, i.e. exactly Queen.cs:230-232's `SetMoveImmediate(EnragedState)` (NextMove = state AND MoveStateMachine.ForceCurrentState(state), MonsterModel.cs:420-432, which does not append to the state log). The resolution-time substitution inside _burn_bright is gone. EXECUTED on a real QUEEN_BOSS combat: with the Queen telegraphing BURN_BRIGHT_FOR_ME_MOVE, killing the Torch Head Amalgam flips the telegraph to ENRAGE_MOVE (intent BUFF) on the spot. WAS: no listener at all, so the Queen kept showing a Defend intent she would not perform. HasAmalgamDied / Amalgam = null stay derived state (_amalgam_died reads the combat), and the three presentation statements (the 'queen_progress' music parameter, the amalgamDeathSpeakLine bark, the spine track reset) stay out of scope by this record's own presentation waivers.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node against Queen.cs:132-162. Six MoveStates with matching ids (PUPPET_STRINGS_MOVE / YOU_ARE_MINE_MOVE / BURN_BRIGHT_FOR_ME_MOVE / OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD_MOVE / EXECUTION_MOVE / ENRAGE_MOVE) and TWO ConditionalBranchStates with matching ids (YOURE_MINE_NOW_BRANCH, BURN_BRIGHT_FOR_ME_BRANCH). Wiring matches exactly: PUPPET -> YOU_ARE_MINE -> mine_branch; BURN_BRIGHT -> burn_branch; OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD -> EXECUTION -> ENRAGE -> OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD (Queen.cs:143-152 vs queen.py:161-170, was :138-147). Both branches carry the SAME two arms in the SAME order -- BURN_BRIGHT when the amalgam lives, OFF_WITH_YOUR_HEAD when it has died (Queen.cs:145-149 vs queen.py:163-167, was :140-144) -- and the duplication is deliberate on both sides. INITIAL state PUPPET_STRINGS_MOVE (Queen.cs:161 vs queen.py:174, was :151). No RandomBranchState anywhere, so there is no AddBranch integer to misread and the Queen draws no MonsterAi entropy. Intents match: CardDebuffIntent -> CARD_DEBUFF; DebuffIntent -> DEBUFF; BuffIntent + DefendIntent -> BUFF also=(DEFEND,); MultiAttackIntent(3, 5) -> ATTACK damage=3 hits=5; SingleAttackIntent(15) -> ATTACK 15; BuffIntent -> BUFF.

guards.what: HasAmalgamDied is a LATCHED flag in C# (Queen.cs:38, 60-71, 226) and a live RECOMPUTE in the sim (queen.py:134-136, was :111-113)
guards.rationale: C# sets the flag once, from AfterDeath, and never clears it; the sim asks `amalgam is None or amalgam.is_gone` every time a branch evaluates. Same observable in every reachable state, and the two ways they could differ were checked rather than assumed. (1) A REVIVE would unlatch the sim and not the game: the sim's three should_die implementers are IllusionPower, SteamEruptionPower and AdaptablePower and no Glory monster applies any of them to the amalgam, so no ported path takes a dead amalgam back to alive. (2) A REMOVED-BUT-ALIVE amalgam would latch the sim and not the game: `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:173-179, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :43-46, same properties moved) and nothing in this fight escapes. C#'s own guard `base.Creature.IsAlive` at Queen.cs:223 only suppresses the latch when the Queen is already dead, which ends the combat on both sides. Concrete trigger that would make this a gap: any ported revive or escape reaching a TorchHeadAmalgam.

guards.what: BurnBrightForMeMove's teammate loop: C# iterates GetTeammatesOf with NO IsAlive filter (Queen.cs:187-191), the sim filters `not enemy.is_removed_from_combat` (queen.py:199-201, re-verified 2026-08-04, was :176-178 `not enemy.is_gone` -- already updated by the Task 28 fix this issue text documents)
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 28.) Both scans now filter on `not enemy.is_removed_from_combat` (membership-only, matching Guardbot.cs:51's `Enemies.Where(c => c.Monster is Fabricator)` and Queen.cs:187-188's teammate walk): a death-vetoed retained corpse (is_gone and retained_after_death, set through the real should_remove_from_combat_after_death hook) is now a valid target in both, while ordinarily killed/escaped creatures stay excluded. Witness: test/test_monster_tier_families.py::TestRetainedCorpseInScan (constructs the corpse via the sim's retention machinery, not a hand-set flag).  The text it replaced read: Queen.cs:187-188 is `CombatState.GetTeammatesOf(Creature).ToList().Where(t => t != Creature)` -- membership of the enemy side is the only test. A creature whose removal was vetoed (the death-is-not-removal case) stays on the side at 0 HP and would still be handed +1 Strength. The sim's enemies list retains every corpse, so the port must filter, and it filters on `is_gone` (superseded historical text; NOW `is_removed_from_combat` per the Task 28 fix quoted above), which also excludes the retained corpse C# would include. SAME MECHANISM and same verdict as monster/guardbot's GuardMove target-set guard (governing rule 3). DORMANT with the trigger named: no ported power sets `retained_after_death` on a TorchHeadAmalgam, and the branch only reaches Burn Bright while the amalgam is alive anyway, so the filter cannot fire on a corpse today. The self-exclusion `t != Creature` matches the sim's `enemy is not self`.
